name: SocialSlider Group Circling
summary: In social VR, the user points at a group of avatars and draws a circle around them in the air with the controller; releasing the trigger selects the whole group, for example to make them transparent.
howItWorks: Built for Oculus Rift with Touch controllers as part of SocialSlider, which changes the transparency of other avatars. While holding the right trigger, the user points at a group and draws a circle around it in mid-air; a gesture recogniser detects the circle and releasing the trigger confirms the selection, with outlines showing the selected avatars. The same system offers ray selection of single avatars, a sweeping line gesture to select everyone, and pointing at oneself to select a predefined group. In a study with 24 participants in a virtual exhibition with 43 avatars, circling, single-avatar raycasting and select-all had similar high usability (median SUS 83), while pointing at oneself scored lower.
advantages: Selects a whole co-located group with one gesture.
Rated as usable as single-target raycasting.
limitations: Usability only; no time or accuracy measured.
Relies on gesture recognition of the drawn circle.

relationships.note: Compared with ray selection of single avatars.
